timing.summary: The combined CHARBOUND|STRIPCC marker behavior became reachable in the library after the change. The fixed old harness still never selects both flags.

coverage_evidence.dependency_reason: The complete before regression-test body lacks the added combined-option cases.
The added cases specify the changed combined-option behavior.

claims.necessity_reason: After the change, combined-option mapping can retain markers for surviving graphemes and remove a boundary before a stripped control. No fixed harness call selects that combination.

before.requirement: The same retained-marker and boundary-removal capability was not available: STRIPCC removed negative boundary sentinels, and there was no branch to remove a boundary preceding a stripped control.
before.reason: The old source accepted the option combination but could not produce this specific behavior. The absence of the new regression test alone is not the basis for this assessment.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: CHARBOUND creates the negative boundary sentinel that old STRIPCC removed.
Reencoding normalized the buffer before converting any surviving sentinel to an output marker.
The complete before regression-test body provides context for the added tests.

after.requirement: Mapping a valid control-containing string with CHARBOUND|STRIPCC must retain markers for surviving graphemes and remove the boundary before a stripped control.
after.reason: Normalization now retains negative sentinels and removes a preceding boundary when it strips a control with CHARBOUND selected. The old harness never selects both flags.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Mapping passes the selected options through decomposition and reencoding.
Reencoding invokes normalization and encodes surviving boundary sentinels.

claims.comparison_reason: The obligation is the same combined-option output capability on both sides. Before, the old implementation removed its marker sentinels; after, the capability exists but the fixed harness options block coverage.
